title: "Predicting pre-diabetes under class imbalance"

```{r include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE,warning = FALSE,message = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(themis)
library(future)
theme_set(theme_classic())
theme_update(plot.title = element_text(hjust = .5))
df <- read_csv("data/Dataset of Diabetes.csv") |> 
  select(-c(ID, No_Pation)) |> 
  mutate(Gender = tolower(Gender),
         CLASS = str_trim(CLASS)) |> 
  distinct()
```

There are 1000 patients and cover three classes (Diabetic, Non-Diabetic, and Predicted-Diabetic). The group in predicted class do not yet meet the clinical threshold for a diabetes diagnosis, but based on expert assessment, or risk factor profiles, they are likely to develop diabetes in the near future. 

Our ami is to develop a model for predictive modeling for the people who are not yet diagnose as diabetic but can develop in near future. Here We are having the class imbalance problem with only 53 are predicted diabetic cases.

```{r}
df |> 
  count(CLASS) |> 
  mutate(prop = prop.table(n),
         label = glue::glue("{n} ({round(prop*100,2)}%)")) |> 
  ggplot(aes(CLASS,prop)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = CLASS), show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label),nudge_y = .05) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "Bar plot for showing the distribution of the response variable",
       y = "Percentage (%)") 
```
Here we are showing the boxplot for the numerical predictors with respect to the predictors. As here we can see there exists significant amount of outliers for each of the continuous variable. For visualization purpose we transformed some of the predictors into log scale.
```{r}
df |> 
  select(CLASS,where(is.numeric)) |> 
  mutate_at(c("VLDL","HDL","Urea","TG","Cr"),log) |> 
  rename_at(c("VLDL","HDL","Urea","TG","Cr"),.funs = \(x) glue::glue("{x} (log transfromed)")) |> 
  pivot_longer(-CLASS) |> 
  ggplot(aes(CLASS, value, fill = CLASS)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE,outlier.alpha = .1) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Boxplot for showing the distribution of the predictors \nwith respecrt to the response.",
       y = "")
```


```{r}
df |> 
  select_if(is.numeric) |> 
  cor() |> 
  as.data.frame() |> 
  rownames_to_column() |> 
  pivot_longer(-rowname) |> 
  ggplot(aes(rowname,name, fill = value, label = round(value,2))) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(limits = c(-1,1),low = "darkred",mid = "white",high = "darkgreen") +
  labs(title = "Correlation plot for the numerical predictors", x = "", y = "", fill = "Corr")
```

```{r}
df |> 
  count(Gender,CLASS) |> 
  group_by(CLASS) ->
  temp; temp |> 
  bind_rows(
    group_by(temp, Gender) |> 
      summarise(n = sum(n),
                CLASS = "Overall")
  ) |> 
  mutate(prop = prop.table(n),
         label = glue::glue("{n} ({round(prop*100,1)}%)"),
         CLASS = factor(x = CLASS,levels = c("N", "P", "Y", "Overall")),
         ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(CLASS,n, fill = Gender, label = label)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_text(aes(y = n + 15), position = position_dodge(width = .9),size = 3) +
  theme(legend.position = c(.2,.8),legend.direction = "horizontal") +
  labs(title = "Barplot for showing the distribution of the response \nwith respect to the predictor Class",
       y = "Count")
```

```{r}
  distinct(distinct,.keep_all = TRUE) |> 
  select(-distinct) |> 
  unnest() |> 
  mutate(facet = map2_chr(.x = var_x,.y = var_y,.f = \(x,y) glue::glue("{x} vs {y}"))
         ) |>

       x = "Var 1", y = "Var 2")
```


## Train Test Split

We are using 75% of the data into training. That is 619 of the data set is the part of the training data and rest of the 207 observation is the part of the testing data.
```{r}
set.seed(1034)
df_split <- initial_split(df,prop = .75, strata = CLASS)
df_vfold <- vfold_cv(training(df_split),strata = CLASS)

eval_mat <- metric_set(accuracy,bal_accuracy,f_meas,precision,recall,spec,sens)

training(df_split) |> 
  count(CLASS) |> 
  mutate(train = prop.table(n)) |> 
  rename(`n(train)` = n) |> 
  bind_cols(
    testing(df_split) |> 
    count(CLASS) |> 
    mutate(test = prop.table(n)) |> 
    rename(`n(test)` = n) |> 
    select(-CLASS)
  ) |> 
  pander::pander()
```

```{r}
df_model <- tibble(model_config = list.files("./model/")) |> 
  mutate(model = str_extract(string = model_config,pattern = "_.*_"),
         model = str_remove_all(model,"_"),
         config = str_extract(model_config,pattern = "_[a-z]+\\."),
         config = str_remove_all(config,"\\.|_")) |> 
  mutate(model_performance = map(.x = model_config,.f = \(model_name) {
    model <- read_rds(here::here(".","model",model_name))
    model |> 
      collect_predictions() |> 
      roc_auc(truth = CLASS,
              c(.pred_N, .pred_P, .pred_Y), 
              estimator = "macro_weighted") |> 
      bind_rows(
        collect_predictions(model) |> 
      eval_mat(truth = CLASS,estimate = .pred_class)
      )}
    )) |> 
  unnest()
```

```{r}
df_model |> 
   select(model,config,.metric,.estimate) |>
  mutate(config = factor(config,c("baseline","under","over","smote","adasyn"))) |> 
  ggplot(aes(config,.estimate,col = model)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(aes(group = model), alpha = .5) +
  facet_wrap(~.metric) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30,vjust = .9),
        legend.position = c(.8,.05)) 

ggsave(filename = "plotForModel.pdf")
```





## Multinomial Logistic Regression Model

BaseLine:
```{r eval=FALSE}
plan(multisession, workers = parallel::detectCores() - 2)
mn_model <- multinom_reg(mode = "classification") |> set_engine("nnet")


df_recipe_up <- recipe(x = training(df_split),formula = CLASS ~ .) |> 
  step_string2factor(CLASS,Gender) 

temp_wf <- workflow() |> 
  add_model(spec = mn_model) |> 
  add_recipe(df_recipe_up) 

mn_model <- temp_wf |> 
  last_fit(split = df_split)

write_rds(x = mn_model,file = "./model/model_mn_baseline.rds")
```

```{r}
mn_model <- read_rds(file = "./model/model_mn_baseline.rds")
mn_model |> 
  collect_predictions() |>
  conf_mat(truth = CLASS,estimate = .pred_class)
```

Oversampling technique: A oversampling ratio of 0.7573054 is selected as the optimal.

```{r eval=FALSE}
plan(multisession, workers = parallel::detectCores() - 2)
mn_model <- multinom_reg(mode = "classification") |> set_engine("nnet")


df_recipe_up <- recipe(x = training(df_split),formula = CLASS ~ .) |> 
  step_string2factor(CLASS,Gender) |>
  step_upsample(CLASS,over_ratio = tune(),seed = 6883)

temp_wf <- workflow() |> 
  add_model(spec = mn_model) |> 
  add_recipe(df_recipe_up) 

set.seed(6883)
grid <- grid_random(x = parameters(over_ratio(range = c(.5,1))), size = 10)

grid_result <- tune_grid(object = temp_wf,resamples = df_vfold,grid = grid,control = control_grid(verbose = TRUE,save_pred = TRUE),metrics = metric_set(roc_auc))

temp_wf <- temp_wf |> 
  finalize_workflow(parameters = select_best(grid_result))

mn_model <- temp_wf |> 
  last_fit(split = df_split)

write_rds(x = mn_model,file = "./model/model_mn_over.rds")
```

```{r}
mn_model <- read_rds(file = "./model/model_mn_over.rds")
mn_model |> 
  collect_predictions() |>
  conf_mat(truth = CLASS,estimate = .pred_class)
```

Undersampling technique: A undersampling ratio of 2.550517 is selected as the optimal.


## Decision Tree Model

BaseLine:
```{r eval=FALSE}
plan(multisession, workers = parallel::detectCores() - 2)
dt_model <- decision_tree(mode = "classification", cost_complexity = tune(), tree_depth = tune(), min_n = tune()) |> set_engine("rpart")


df_recipe_up <- recipe(x = training(df_split),formula = CLASS ~ .) |> 
  step_string2factor(CLASS,Gender) 

temp_wf <- workflow() |> 
  add_model(spec = dt_model) |> 
  add_recipe(df_recipe_up) 

set.seed(3461)
grid <- grid_random(x = parameters(cost_complexity(), tree_depth(), min_n()), size = 10)

grid_result <- tune_grid(object = temp_wf,resamples = df_vfold,grid = grid,control = control_grid(verbose = TRUE,save_pred = TRUE),metrics = metric_set(roc_auc))

temp_wf <- temp_wf |> 
  finalize_workflow(parameters = select_best(grid_result))

dt_model <- temp_wf |> 
  last_fit(split = df_split)
```
